question: Why does the separateness of śakti from its holder not amount to difference?
premises: Śakti is indeed undivided from the power-holder.
Thereby this separateness does not indeed amount to difference.
Where knowerhood is absent no śakti exists, so such a nature is not power-endowed.
inference: Śakti, knower, and power-holder entail one another, so their separateness is not difference.
uncertainties: The segmentation of tenaiti as tena-plus-eti against tena-plus-iti.
The exact scope of our in ca no.
plain_english: And śakti, for our part, is undivided from the power-holder; thereby this separateness does not indeed amount to difference. Where knowerhood is absent, moreover, no śakti exists — so such a nature is not endowed with power.
